live.instructions: Square Yards real-estate data for INDIA ONLY (cities, localities, projects, listings, price rates across India; powered by Square Yards). Do NOT use these tools for real estate outside India — say so and decline for other countries. Use search_entities FIRST to resolve a place or brand (city/locality/micromarket/builder/landmark); it returns each entity with ready-to-use `forProperties` and `forProjects` scopes. Then call search_properties (sale/rent listings — set listingType) or search_projects (new developments), passing the chosen entity's scope verbatim. Budgets are absolute INR. For a deep detail a search result did NOT include (a project's possession/completion date, per-wing RERA, amenities, full spec), drill down with get_entity_details using an id from the search result. To compare 2-4 entities of the SAME type side by side (two projects, three localities), use compare_entities with their ids. To RANK many localities — or a city's top areas — for end-use vs investment ("which area is best to buy in") use recommend_localities (resolve the locality ids via search_entities first). For informational "how/what" questions (home loans, vastu, buying/renting process) use search_faq; for EMI or affordability NUMBERS ("EMI on 80 lakh", "what can I afford on 2L/month") use estimate_home_loan; for area/land unit conversions ("how many sq ft in a bigha", "5 acre to gaj") use area_conversion. Both are pure calculators. All tools are read-only and never mutate data.

tools.name: search_entities
tools.title: Resolve Place, Builder or Project
tools.description:
Resolve a place/builder/project NAME (city, locality, micromarket, builder, project, landmark) into the ids the other tools need; returns ranked entity SUMMARIES, never full listings/projects. For a normal search BY PLACE do NOT call this first -> call search_properties or search_projects with `location` set (they resolve the place themselves in ONE call). Use search_entities ONLY to disambiguate an ambiguous place, get a landmark's coordinates, or resolve a builder/project name to an id. When you do use it, chain in the SAME turn: resolving a place but fetching no listings/projects/detail is INCOMPLETE.

Reading results:
- city/locality/micromarket/builder -> carries ready-made `forProperties` (beats-space ids -> search_properties) and `forProjects` (dotcom-space ids -> search_projects) scope objects; pass the matching one's fields VERBATIM, never build or transform ids.
- type:"project" -> take its `dotcomId`; drill in with get_entity_details (entity="project") or scope search_projects by it.
- type:"landmark" -> take its `coordinates` as lat/long (or landmarkId "lat|lng|name") for a near-<landmark> radius search.

Routing after resolving: resale/rent -> search_properties; new-construction -> search_projects; general buy -> BOTH; one entity's full detail or a place's price-rates -> get_entity_details. Always pick the ONE result whose name and city match the user's words ("Noida" -> the city Noida, not Greater Noida). (search_faq answers how/what/why and needs no id.)

q.description: Free-text place, brand, or PROJECT name in the user's own words (required).

entityType.description: Optional comma list to scope result types: city, locality, micromarket, builder, project, landmark. Omit for all types. Use entityType="project" to resolve a PROJECT NAME to its id (then drill into get_entity_details or search_projects). Use entityType="landmark" to get a place's coordinates for a near-by radius search.

cityHint.description: City NAME to bias ranking toward when the query is ambiguous (e.g. a bare "Sector 15"). Matching-city results float to the top; nothing is dropped. Pass the user's city when known.

cityId.description: Dotcom city id(s), comma-separated. Restrict results to these cities.

beatsCityId.description: Beats-space city id(s), comma-separated. OR'd with cityId.

tools.name: search_properties
tools.title: Search Property Listings
tools.description: Search actual SALE or RENT LISTINGS - individual resale/rental units, shown as property cards. ROUTING: listing intent ("flats/for sale/resale/to rent") -> THIS; "project/new launch/under construction" -> search_projects; a general buy with no resale-vs-new preference -> call BOTH (this with Sale + search_projects); a PLACE's price rates / per-sq-ft / market trends (not individual units) -> get_entity_details entity="property-rates" (NOT a listings search). ALWAYS set listingType (Sale|Rent). SIMPLEST (one call): pass `location` as the place in the user's words ("Gurgaon") plus filters - it auto-resolves the place, so do NOT call search_entities first. For precise scope pass an entity's `forProperties` ids (cityId/subLocalityId/microMarketId = BEATS ids) VERBATIM; explicit ids or lat/long override `location`; never guess numeric ids and never reuse a `forProjects`/dotcom id (different id space). budget = absolute INR (40 lakh -> 4000000); area in sq ft; bedrooms = BHK label ("2 BHK"). propertyTypeName takes EXACT propertyType values (Apartment, Villa, Builder Floor, Independent House, Office Space, Shop, Plot, ...) - "Studio"/"1 RK"/"Ind Floor" are bedrooms (unitType) values, NOT types. With NO propertyTypeName the search defaults to RESIDENTIAL types - set a commercial type explicitly for offices/shops (project-scoped searches exempt). A geo search (lat/long or landmark) adds `distanceInKm` per card. Results follow Square Yards ranking; promoted cards carry isFeatured/isExclusive flags (use `sort` for price/newest order). Each card carries a normalized pricePerSqft (₹/sq.ft) + areaSqft so "cheapest per sq.ft" is directly answerable; a dataQualityFlag caveats an implausible area/price. For "what EMI would this cost" pass a card price to estimate_home_loan. DRILL-DOWN: every listing has an `id` -> get_entity_details entity="listing" id=that `id`, copied verbatim (never the title or URL).

listingType.description: Sale or Rent listings. ALWAYS set this.

location.description: Free-text place in the user's words — "Gurgaon", "Sector 43 Gurgaon", "Whitefield Bangalore". The tool resolves it to the right city/locality internally, so you can search in ONE call without first calling search_entities. Ignored if you pass explicit scope ids (cityId/…) or lat/long. Prefer this for a simple place-based search.

cityHint.description: City to disambiguate an ambiguous `location` (a bare "Sector 15" exists in many cities). Pass the user's city when known. If `location` matches multiple cities and no hint is given, the result comes back `ambiguous:true` with a `candidates` list so you can ask which city.

cityId.description: City id — BEATS id space. Use an entity's `forProperties.cityId` VERBATIM; never reuse a `forProjects`/dotcom city id here (the two searches use different id spaces).

propertyTypeName.description: EXACT propertyType value(s), comma-separated — e.g. "Apartment,Villa". Use only real types: Apartment, Builder Floor, Independent House, Villa, Penthouse, Townhouse, Plot, Office Space, Shop, Showroom. NOT "Studio"/"Ind Floor"/"1 RK" — those are bedrooms (unitType) values and match nothing here. Omit it with bedrooms set to get the residential default.

bedrooms.description: BHK/unit label(s), comma-separated — e.g. "2 BHK,3 BHK", "Studio", "1 RK". This filters unit type, NOT propertyType.

minPrice.description: Min total price, absolute INR (40 lakh → 4000000).

maxPrice.description: Max total price, absolute INR (1 cr → 10000000).

amenityName.description: Amenity filter — comma-separated amenity names, plain text, case-insensitive, matched as an exact PHRASE (not fuzzy). Pass the SHORT, singular, punctuation-free core term: "swimming pool", "gymnasium", "security", "cctv", "power backup", "lift", "kids play", "clubhouse", "indoor games". A short term still matches a longer catalog entry ("security" matches "24 x 7 Security"). Multiple names are AND-ed (results must have ALL of them); for "X or Y" run two searches and merge. NOTE: amenity data is sparse (older/resale stock often has none) — if a search returns few/zero results, retry with fewer amenities, then none, and say the amenity data may be unavailable.

amenityDetail.description: Optional: comma-separated NUMERIC amenity ids — only if you already hold canonical ids for THIS tool. Ids are NOT shared between the properties and projects searches; never copy an id from the other tool. Prefer amenityName.

lat.description: Latitude for a geo-radius search (each result then carries `distanceInKm`).

landmarkId.description: Landmark as "lat|lng|name" for a radius search (parsed into lat/long). Get it from a search_entities landmark result's coordinates — lets "near <landmark>" work for listings.

sort.description: Sort order (default relevance). price_low excludes price-on-request.

countryId.description: Ranking country; defaults to 1 = India. This server is INDIA-focused — leave unset. (8 = UAE exists only for the rare Square Yards Dubai listing; do not use it for a general non-India request — decline those.)

sort_key.description: Advanced raw sort key (takes precedence over `sort`).

tools.name: search_projects
tools.title: Search New-Construction Projects
tools.description: Search NEW-CONSTRUCTION projects/developments (NOT resale listings) - under-construction, new-launch, ready-to-move, upcoming - returned as project cards (developer, price band, BHK configs, status, RERA). ROUTING: pick THIS for "project/new launch/under construction"; use search_properties for resale/rental listings; for a general buy intent with no new-vs-resale preference call BOTH in the same turn. SIMPLEST PATH (one call): pass `location` as the place in the user's words ("Noida", "Wakad Pune") plus filters - it resolves the place itself, so you need NOT call search_entities first. For precise/repeat scope you may instead pass an entity's `forProjects` ids (cityId/localityId/micromarketId/builderId - DOTCOM id space) VERBATIM; explicit ids override `location`. Never reuse a search_properties BEATS id here, and never guess ids. SPECIFIC NAMED project: do NOT use this discovery list (a city-scoped search returns the wrong project) - resolve the name via search_entities (entityType="project"), take its `dotcomId`, and open it with get_entity_details (entity="project", id=that dotcomId). A geo (lat/long or landmark) search adds `distanceInKm` per card. Defaults: RESIDENTIAL projects unless buildingType=2 (commercial) or a type/q is set; default order is "Top Selling" (Square Yards promoted/featured ranking - cards carry isFocus/isAssured/hasExclusive flags; use `sort` for price/connectivity order). A card price + estimate_home_loan gives its EMI. DRILL-DOWN: every card has an `id` - for possession/completion date, per-wing RERA, amenities or full spec call get_entity_details (entity="project", id=that `id` verbatim - never the name/slug).

location.description: Free-text place in the user's words — "Noida", "Sector 150 Noida", "Wakad Pune". The tool resolves it to the right city/locality internally, so you can search in ONE call without first calling search_entities. Ignored if you pass explicit scope ids (cityId/…) or lat/long. Prefer this for a simple place-based search.

cityHint.description: City to disambiguate an ambiguous `location` (a bare "Sector 150" exists in many cities). Pass the user's city when known. If `location` matches multiple cities and no hint is given, the result comes back `ambiguous:true` with a `candidates` list so you can ask which city.

cityId.description: City id — DOTCOM id space. Use an entity's `forProjects.cityId` VERBATIM; never reuse a `forProperties`/beats city id here (the two searches use different id spaces).

possesion.description: Expected COMPLETION YEAR(s) — the possession DATE filter (note the single "s"). Comma-separated 4-digit years, e.g. "2026" or "2026,2027". Use for timeframe phrasing ("possession by 2027", "ready in 2026", "handover next year") — resolve relative phrases to absolute years (today is mid-2026). Independent of possessionStatus and combines with it.

amenityName.description: Amenity filter — comma-separated amenity names, plain text, case-insensitive, matched as an exact PHRASE (not fuzzy). Pass the SHORT, singular, punctuation-free core term: "swimming pool", "gymnasium", "security", "cctv", "power backup", "lift", "kids play", "clubhouse", "indoor games". A short term still matches a longer catalog entry ("security" matches "24 x 7 Security"). Multiple names are AND-ed (results must have ALL of them); for "X or Y" run two searches and merge. NOTE: amenity data is sparse — if a search returns few/zero results, retry with fewer amenities, then none, and say the amenity data may be unavailable.

amenityDetail.description: Optional: comma-separated NUMERIC amenity ids — only if you already hold canonical ids for THIS tool. Ids are NOT shared between the projects and properties searches; never copy an id from the other tool. Prefer amenityName.

more.description: Feature filters, comma-separated — e.g. "Rera Registered Projects".

landmarkId.description: Landmark as "lat|lng|name" for a radius search (coordinates from a search_entities landmark result). Commas separate MULTIPLE landmarks here, so use pipes within one.

possessionStatus.description: Construction STAGE filter, comma list of: new_launch | under_construction | ready_to_move. Stage phrasing: "newly launched", "under construction", "ready to move". Combines with `possesion` (year), e.g. under_construction + possesion=2027. Do NOT pair new_launch with a near-term year (usually empty). Omit if the user gives no possession constraint. NOTE: "upcoming"/pre-launch and "stalled"/on-hold are NOT search-filterable (the endpoint ignores them) — do not pass them; for a specific project's on-hold details use get_entity_details (fields="stalledData").

sortBy.description: Advanced raw sort key (takes precedence over `sort`).

tools.name: get_entity_details
tools.title: Get Entity Details & Rates
tools.description: Fetch FULL DETAIL for ONE entity by numeric id - the last drill-down step. Use ONLY when the search tools (search_properties / search_projects / search_entities) did not already answer: a project's possession/completion date, per-wing RERA, amenities or spec; a listing's full attributes; a locality's price rates & pros/cons. For how/what/why questions (loans, vastu, process) use search_faq, not this. You MUST already hold the id from a prior result - never guess an id or slug; if you only have a NAME, call the matching search tool FIRST and copy its id (pick the one whose name+city matches; else say so). Which id, by entity: listing -> a search_properties result's `id`; project -> a search_projects result's `id`, OR a search_entities `type:"project"` result's `dotcomId` (project has one id space); developer -> a search_entities `type:"builder"` result's `dotcomId`; city/locality/micromarket -> a search_entities result's `beatsId` (default) or `dotcomId` (then set idType="dotcom"). For projects the result includes `possessionStartingFrom`, the authoritative possession date (earliest upcoming RERA completion). For a PLACE's PRICE / PROPERTY RATES / market insights use entity="property-rates": resolve the place via search_entities, take its `beatsId`, then call with entity="property-rates", rateType=(city|locality|micromarket) and id=that beatsId. Optional `fields` adds sections (comma-separated); omit for the primary detail. Returns a compact, intent-filtered detail object.

entity.description: The entity type to fetch detail for. Use "property-rates" for a CITY / LOCALITY / MICROMARKET's price, rates or market-insight page (market overview, price trends, locality/micromarket rates, rental rates, top projects + an AI narrative) — it ALSO requires `rateType` and the place's BEATS id (resolve it via search_entities first).

id.description:
The entity's NUMERIC id (e.g. "8761"), copied VERBATIM from a prior tool result — NEVER a name, slug, or guess ("piramal-revanta" is wrong). EXACTLY which field to copy, by entity:
• listing → the `id` field of a search_properties result.
• project → the `id` field of a search_projects result, OR a search_entities result whose type is "project" — use its `dotcomId` (project has a single id space; idType is not needed).
• developer → a search_entities result whose type is "builder" — use its `dotcomId`.
• city / locality / micromarket → a search_entities result of that type — use its `beatsId` (idType=beats, the default) or `dotcomId` (idType=dotcom).
If you only have a NAME, call the matching search tool FIRST and copy the id from the result you want — do not construct or transform it. Pick the result whose name (and city) matches the user's words before copying its id; if nothing clearly matches, say so rather than drilling a different entity.

idType.description: Which id space the id is from. Default beats. ONLY affects city/locality/micromarket (which have both id spaces). Ignored for developer/project/listing (single id) and property-rates (always beats). Pass dotcom when the id came from a dotcom-keyed field.

rateType.description: REQUIRED when entity="property-rates" (ignored otherwise): which kind of place the rate record is for — a city, locality, or micromarket (there is NO project rate page). Combined with the BEATS `id` it forms the key — e.g. rateType="city" + id="59" → Gurgaon city rates; rateType="micromarket" + id="154" → Vijayawada Central. Get the beats id by calling search_entities for the place FIRST and taking its `beatsId`.

fields.description: Optional top-level section(s) to return, COMMA-SEPARATED (e.g. "projectData,reraData"). Omit for the primary detail section, which already answers most questions. Examples — project: projectData (default; includes status, price, RERA wings + derived possessionStartingFrom), landmarks (nearby schools/hospitals/banks/metro by distance), reraData, keyAspects, stalledData. listing: listingData, landmarks (nearby points of interest by distance). city: cityData, topDevelopers, landmarks. locality/micromarket: localityOverviewData, insightsData, nearByLocalitiesV2, landmarks. developer: developerData. property-rates: propertyRatesData (structured rates) is the DEFAULT; add propertyRatesAiData to fields ONLY when the user wants the prose narrative (it is heavy and restates the numbers) — e.g. fields="propertyRatesData,propertyRatesAiData".

tools.name: compare_entities
tools.title: Compare Entities
tools.description: Compare 2-4 entities of the SAME type side by side (two projects, three localities, two listings), rendered as a comparison table. Pick this over calling get_entity_details repeatedly when the user asks to compare or contrast named places or properties. All items must share one `entity`, and you must already hold each numeric `id`: resolve each first via search_entities / search_properties / search_projects, never guessing. For city/locality/micromarket set `idType` to the id's source (beats default, or dotcom); it is ignored for project/listing. Cross-type comparison is not supported, and property-rates is not comparable. To RANK many localities or answer "which area is best" use recommend_localities.

entity.description: Entity type — the SAME for every item.

id.description: The entity's NUMERIC id, copied verbatim from a prior search/detail result.

idType.description: Id space (city/locality/micromarket only); default beats. Ignored otherwise.

items.description: The 2–4 entities to compare, ALL of the same `entity` type (e.g. two projects, or three localities). Resolve each id first via search_entities / search_properties / search_projects.

tools.name: recommend_localities
tools.title: Recommend & Rank Localities
tools.description: Rank 2-20 localities (or a city's top localities) for END-USE vs INVESTMENT, as a scored list. ROUTING: pick THIS when the user names MANY areas or asks for "the best area(s)" / a recommendation (compare_entities is only a 2-4 side-by-side TABLE and never ranks). Resolve each locality NAME to an id via search_entities (entityType="locality") FIRST, then pass `localities:[{id,idType}]` (or `cityId` to rank a city's top localities). Optional `budget` (absolute INR) flags each `inBudget`; `goal` = end_use | investment | both (default). HONEST + deterministic: it only combines signals get_entity_details already returns and NEVER invents a verdict. Sub-scores (0-100): connectivity/lifestyle/livability = the backend 0-5 index x20; appreciation = price-trend % (0%->50, +/-12.5%->100/0); liquidity (govt registered-deal volume) + value (rental yield) are ranked RELATIVE to the set. Weights - end-use: livability .35, connectivity .30, lifestyle .25, value .10; investment: appreciation .40, liquidity .30, value .20, connectivity .10; overall = their mean. A missing signal is OMITTED (not zero-filled), BUT a locality is only RANKED when present signals cover >50% of the goal's CORE (discriminating) weight — investment = appreciation/liquidity/yield (connectivity alone can't rank it), end-use = livability/connectivity/lifestyle; thinner ones go to `insufficientData` (with known signals + reason), so a one-signal locality can never top the list. signalCoverage is that CORE-weight share (0-1); each item also carries signalsUsed + raw numbers (avgRate, rentalYield, priceTrendPct, transactions) and VERBATIM pros/cons. India only, read-only.

id.description: The locality NUMERIC id, from a search_entities locality result.

idType.description: Id space of `id` (default beats). Pass "dotcom" when the id came from a dotcom-keyed field.

localities.description: The 2–20 localities to rank, each { id, idType? }. Resolve names → ids via search_entities (entityType="locality") FIRST; never guess. Provide this OR `cityId`.

cityId.description: Instead of an explicit list, rank the CITY's top localities (up to 15). A city id from search_entities. Ignored when `localities` is given.

budget.description: Optional purchase budget, absolute INR (e.g. {min:20000000,max:30000000}). Flags each locality `inBudget` when a real project there fits — never a hard filter.

bedrooms.description: Optional BHK context, e.g. "3 BHK" (echoed; the ranking is locality-level).

goal.description: Which composite sorts the result: end_use (livability/connectivity), investment (appreciation/liquidity/yield), or both (default).

tools.name: search_faq
tools.title: Search Real-Estate FAQ
tools.description: Answer INFORMATIONAL/advisory real-estate questions -- buying/renting/selling process, home loans, legal, RERA rights, NRI purchases, Azuro-managed rentals -- from the bundled Square Yards FAQ corpus. Pick this for general how/what/why questions; needs NO id, does NOT touch listings/projects. Do NOT use it to find inventory (use search_entities -> search_properties/search_projects), for a PLACE-specific price/rates question (use get_entity_details entity="property-rates"), or for EMI/affordability NUMBERS (use estimate_home_loan, not this). Optionally pass `category` (e.g. buying/renting/selling) to scope results; `top_k` caps returned Q/A pairs (default 3).

query.description: An informational question, e.g. "what credit score do I need for a home loan".

category.description: Optional: scope the search to one FAQ category (e.g. "buying", "renting", "selling"). Matched on the category id or label, case-insensitive. If it does not match a known category the filter is ignored and a note lists the valid ones.

tools.name: estimate_home_loan
tools.title: Home Loan EMI & Affordability Calculator
tools.description: Calculate a home-loan EMI, or estimate how much a buyer can afford, for INDIA home loans. mode="emi": given loanAmount (or propertyPrice + down payment) + rate + tenure, returns the monthly EMI, total interest and total payable. mode="affordability": given monthly/annual NET income (+ existing EMIs, optional down-payment cash), returns the max EMI capacity, max loan and max property price via FOIR + RBI LTV tiers. Use THIS for any loan NUMBERS question ("EMI on X", "what can I afford on Y salary", "how much down payment do I need") — e.g. turn a listing/project card price into an EMI. For loan PROCESS/documents/eligibility prose use search_faq instead. Pure calculator: no ids, no live data. Money is absolute INR (1.2 Cr → 12000000). Defaults: 8.75% p.a., 20-year tenure, FOIR 0.50, stamp+registration ≈6%. Results are indicative with the disclaimer included — never present them as a loan offer.

mode.description: "emi" = monthly payment for a known loan/price; "affordability" = max budget from income.

loanAmount.description: emi mode: loan principal in absolute INR (₹80L → 8000000). Wins over propertyPrice.

propertyPrice.description: emi mode: property price in absolute INR — the loan is price minus down payment.

downPayment.description: emi mode: down payment in absolute INR (used with propertyPrice).

downPaymentPercent.description: emi mode: down payment as % of propertyPrice; used when downPayment is absent. If neither is given the RBI-minimum down payment for the price band is assumed.

monthlyIncome.description: affordability mode: NET take-home income per month, absolute INR (₹2L → 200000).

annualIncome.description: affordability mode: NET annual income, absolute INR (divided by 12 internally).

existingEmi.description: affordability mode: existing monthly EMI obligations, INR (default 0).

foir.description: affordability mode: share of income lenders allow for all EMIs (default 0.50; clamped 0.3–0.6).

downPaymentAvailable.description: affordability mode: cash available for down payment + costs — caps the max property price.

includeTxnCosts.description: Include ~6% stamp duty + registration in the cash estimates (default true).

tools.name: area_conversion
tools.title: Area Unit Converter
tools.description: Convert a land/area measurement between the units used in INDIA — metric (sq metre, sq km, hectare, are, sq cm), imperial (sq feet, sq yard/"gaj", sq inch, acre) and traditional Indian land units (cent, decimal, ground, guntha, marla, kanal, killa, ankanam, bigha, biswa, kattha). Use THIS for any unit-conversion NUMBERS ("how many sq ft in a bigha", "convert 5 acre to gaj", "200 gaj in sq feet"). Pure calculator — no ids, no live data. Pass `value` (a positive number) and `from`; give `to` for a single target, or omit it to get the value in the common units at once. Units accept friendly aliases (sqft, sqm, gaj, acre, cent, ground…). IMPORTANT: bigha, biswa and kattha differ by state, so pass a state-qualified code (BIGHA_PUCCA_UP_I, BISWA_HP_I, KATTHA_BIHAR, …); a bare "bigha" or an unknown unit returns the list of valid codes. For property PRICE/EMI numbers use estimate_home_loan; for live listings use search_properties.

value.description: The area amount to convert — a positive number, e.g. 5 for "5 acre".

from.description: Source unit. Codes or aliases: SQ_M, SQ_FT, SQ_YD ("gaj"), SQ_CM, SQ_IN, SQ_KM, HECTARE, ARE, ACRE, CENT, DECIMAL, GROUND, GUNTHA, MARLA, KANAL, KILLA, ANKANAM; bigha/biswa/kattha are state-qualified (e.g. BIGHA_PUCCA_UP_I, BISWA_HP_I, KATTHA_BIHAR).

to.description: Target unit (same code/alias set). OMIT to get the value in the common units (ft², yd², m², acre, hectare) at once.

tools.title: Resolve Place, Builder or Project
tools.description:
Resolve a place/builder/project NAME (city, locality, micromarket, builder, project, landmark) into the ids the other tools need; returns ranked entity SUMMARIES, never full listings/projects. - type:"project" -> take its `dotcomId`; drill in with get_entity_details (entity="project") or scope search_projects by it.
- type:"landmark" -> take its `coordinates` as lat/long (or landmarkId "lat|lng|name") for a near-<landmark> radius search.

q.description: Free-text place, brand, or PROJECT name in the user's own words (required).

entityType.description: Optional comma list to scope result types: city, locality, micromarket, builder, project, landmark. Omit for all types. Use entityType="project" to resolve a PROJECT NAME to its id (then drill into get_entity_details or search_projects). cityHint.description: City NAME to bias ranking toward when the query is ambiguous (e.g. a bare "Sector 15"). Matching-city results float to the top; nothing is dropped. Pass the user's city when known.

cityId.description: Dotcom city id(s), comma-separated. Restrict results to these cities.

beatsCityId.description: Beats-space city id(s), comma-separated. OR'd with cityId.

tools.name: search_properties
tools.title: Search Property Listings
tools.description: Search actual SALE or RENT LISTINGS - individual resale/rental units, shown as property cards. ROUTING: listing intent ("flats/for sale/resale/to rent") -> THIS; "project/new launch/under construction" -> search_projects; a general buy with no resale-vs-new preference -> call BOTH (this with Sale + search_projects); a PLACE's price rates / per-sq-ft / market trends (not individual units) -> get_entity_details entity="property-rates" (NOT a listings search). ALWAYS set listingType (Sale|Rent). SIMPLEST (one call): pass `location` as the place in the user's words ("Gurgaon") plus filters - it auto-resolves the place, so do NOT call search_entities first. For precise scope pass an entity's `forProperties` ids (cityId/subLocalityId/microMarketId = BEATS ids) VERBATIM; explicit ids or lat/long override `location`; never guess numeric ids and never reuse a `forProjects`/dotcom id (different id space). budget = absolute INR (40 lakh -> 4000000); area in sq ft; bedrooms = BHK label ("2 BHK"). propertyTypeName takes EXACT propertyType values (Apartment, Villa, Builder Floor, Independent House, Office Space, Shop, Plot, ...) - "Studio"/"1 RK"/"Ind Floor" are bedrooms (unitType) values, NOT types. With NO propertyTypeName the search defaults to RESIDENTIAL types - set a commercial type explicitly for offices/shops (project-scoped searches exempt). A geo search (lat/long or landmark) adds `distanceInKm` per card. Results follow Square Yards ranking; promoted cards carry isFeatured/isExclusive flags (use `sort` for price/newest order). Each card carries a normalized pricePerSqft (₹/sq.ft) + areaSqft so "cheapest per sq.ft" is directly answerable; a dataQualityFlag caveats an implausible area/price. For "what EMI would this cost" pass a card price to estimate_home_loan. DRILL-DOWN: every listing has an `id` -> get_entity_details entity="listing" id=that `id`, copied verbatim (never the title or URL).

listingType.description: Sale or Rent listings. ALWAYS set this.

location.description: Free-text place in the user's words — "Gurgaon", "Sector 43 Gurgaon", "Whitefield Bangalore". The tool resolves it to the right city/locality internally, so you can search in ONE call without first calling search_entities. Ignored if you pass explicit scope ids (cityId/…) or lat/long. Prefer this for a simple place-based search.

cityHint.description: City to disambiguate an ambiguous `location` (a bare "Sector 15" exists in many cities). Pass the user's city when known. If `location` matches multiple cities and no hint is given, the result comes back `ambiguous:true` with a `candidates` list so you can ask which city.

cityId.description: City id — BEATS id space. Use an entity's `forProperties.cityId` VERBATIM; never reuse a `forProjects`/dotcom city id here (the two searches use different id spaces).

propertyTypeName.description: EXACT propertyType value(s), comma-separated — e.g. "Apartment,Villa". Use only real types: Apartment, Builder Floor, Independent House, Villa, Penthouse, Townhouse, Plot, Office Space, Shop, Showroom. NOT "Studio"/"Ind Floor"/"1 RK" — those are bedrooms (unitType) values and match nothing here. Omit it with bedrooms set to get the residential default.

bedrooms.description: BHK/unit label(s), comma-separated — e.g. "2 BHK,3 BHK", "Studio", "1 RK". This filters unit type, NOT propertyType.

minPrice.description: Min total price, absolute INR (40 lakh → 4000000).

maxPrice.description: Max total price, absolute INR (1 cr → 10000000).

amenityName.description: Amenity filter — comma-separated amenity names, plain text, case-insensitive, matched as an exact PHRASE (not fuzzy). Pass the SHORT, singular, punctuation-free core term: "swimming pool", "gymnasium", "security", "cctv", "power backup", "lift", "kids play", "clubhouse", "indoor games". A short term still matches a longer catalog entry ("security" matches "24 x 7 Security"). Multiple names are AND-ed (results must have ALL of them); for "X or Y" run two searches and merge. NOTE: amenity data is sparse (older/resale stock often has none) — if a search returns few/zero results, retry with fewer amenities, then none, and say the amenity data may be unavailable.

amenityDetail.description: Optional: comma-separated NUMERIC amenity ids — only if you already hold canonical ids for THIS tool. Ids are NOT shared between the properties and projects searches; never copy an id from the other tool. Prefer amenityName.

lat.description: Latitude for a geo-radius search (each result then carries `distanceInKm`).

landmarkId.description: Landmark as "lat|lng|name" for a radius search (parsed into lat/long). Get it from a search_entities landmark result's coordinates — lets "near <landmark>" work for listings.

sort.description: Sort order (default relevance). price_low excludes price-on-request.

countryId.description: Ranking country; defaults to 1 = India. This server is INDIA-focused — leave unset. (8 = UAE exists only for the rare Square Yards Dubai listing; do not use it for a general non-India request — decline those.)

sort_key.description: Advanced raw sort key (takes precedence over `sort`).

tools.name: search_projects
tools.title: Search New-Construction Projects
tools.description: Search NEW-CONSTRUCTION projects/developments (NOT resale listings) - under-construction, new-launch, ready-to-move, upcoming - returned as project cards (developer, price band, BHK configs, status, RERA). ROUTING: pick THIS for "project/new launch/under construction"; use search_properties for resale/rental listings; for a general buy intent with no new-vs-resale preference call BOTH in the same turn. SIMPLEST PATH (one call): pass `location` as the place in the user's words ("Noida", "Wakad Pune") plus filters - it resolves the place itself, so you need NOT call search_entities first. For precise/repeat scope you may instead pass an entity's `forProjects` ids (cityId/localityId/micromarketId/builderId - DOTCOM id space) VERBATIM; explicit ids override `location`. Never reuse a search_properties BEATS id here, and never guess ids. SPECIFIC NAMED project: do NOT use this discovery list (a city-scoped search returns the wrong project) - resolve the name via search_entities (entityType="project"), take its `dotcomId`, and open it with get_entity_details (entity="project", id=that dotcomId). A geo (lat/long or landmark) search adds `distanceInKm` per card. Defaults: RESIDENTIAL projects unless buildingType=2 (commercial) or a type/q is set; default order is "Top Selling" (Square Yards promoted/featured ranking - cards carry isFocus/isAssured/hasExclusive flags; use `sort` for price/connectivity order). A card price + estimate_home_loan gives its EMI. DRILL-DOWN: every card has an `id` - for possession/completion date, per-wing RERA, amenities or full spec call get_entity_details (entity="project", id=that `id` verbatim - never the name/slug).

location.description: Free-text place in the user's words — "Noida", "Sector 150 Noida", "Wakad Pune". The tool resolves it to the right city/locality internally, so you can search in ONE call without first calling search_entities. Ignored if you pass explicit scope ids (cityId/…) or lat/long. Prefer this for a simple place-based search.

cityId.description: City id — DOTCOM id space. Use an entity's `forProjects.cityId` VERBATIM; never reuse a `forProperties`/beats city id here (the two searches use different id spaces).

possesion.description: Expected COMPLETION YEAR(s) — the possession DATE filter (note the single "s"). Comma-separated 4-digit years, e.g. "2026" or "2026,2027". Use for timeframe phrasing ("possession by 2027", "ready in 2026", "handover next year") — resolve relative phrases to absolute years (today is mid-2026). Independent of possessionStatus and combines with it.

amenityName.description: Amenity filter — comma-separated amenity names, plain text, case-insensitive, matched as an exact PHRASE (not fuzzy). Pass the SHORT, singular, punctuation-free core term: "swimming pool", "gymnasium", "security", "cctv", "power backup", "lift", "kids play", "clubhouse", "indoor games". A short term still matches a longer catalog entry ("security" matches "24 x 7 Security"). Multiple names are AND-ed (results must have ALL of them); for "X or Y" run two searches and merge. NOTE: amenity data is sparse — if a search returns few/zero results, retry with fewer amenities, then none, and say the amenity data may be unavailable.

amenityDetail.description: Optional: comma-separated NUMERIC amenity ids — only if you already hold canonical ids for THIS tool. Ids are NOT shared between the projects and properties searches; never copy an id from the other tool. Prefer amenityName.

more.description: Feature filters, comma-separated — e.g. "Rera Registered Projects".

landmarkId.description: Landmark as "lat|lng|name" for a radius search (coordinates from a search_entities landmark result). Commas separate MULTIPLE landmarks here, so use pipes within one.

possessionStatus.description: Construction STAGE filter, comma list of: new_launch | under_construction | ready_to_move. Stage phrasing: "newly launched", "under construction", "ready to move". Combines with `possesion` (year), e.g. under_construction + possesion=2027. Do NOT pair new_launch with a near-term year (usually empty). Omit if the user gives no possession constraint. NOTE: "upcoming"/pre-launch and "stalled"/on-hold are NOT search-filterable (the endpoint ignores them) — do not pass them; for a specific project's on-hold details use get_entity_details (fields="stalledData").

sortBy.description: Advanced raw sort key (takes precedence over `sort`).

tools.name: get_entity_details
tools.title: Get Entity Details & Rates
tools.description: Fetch FULL DETAIL for ONE entity by numeric id - the last drill-down step. Use ONLY when the search tools (search_properties / search_projects / search_entities) did not already answer: a project's possession/completion date, per-wing RERA, amenities or spec; a listing's full attributes; a locality's price rates & pros/cons. For how/what/why questions (loans, vastu, process) use search_faq, not this. You MUST already hold the id from a prior result - never guess an id or slug; if you only have a NAME, call the matching search tool FIRST and copy its id (pick the one whose name+city matches; else say so). Which id, by entity: listing -> a search_properties result's `id`; project -> a search_projects result's `id`, OR a search_entities `type:"project"` result's `dotcomId` (project has one id space); developer -> a search_entities `type:"builder"` result's `dotcomId`; city/locality/micromarket -> a search_entities result's `beatsId` (default) or `dotcomId` (then set idType="dotcom"). For projects the result includes `possessionStartingFrom`, the authoritative possession date (earliest upcoming RERA completion). For a PLACE's PRICE / PROPERTY RATES / market insights use entity="property-rates": resolve the place via search_entities, take its `beatsId`, then call with entity="property-rates", rateType=(city|locality|micromarket) and id=that beatsId. Optional `fields` adds sections (comma-separated); omit for the primary detail. Returns a compact, intent-filtered detail object.

entity.description: The entity type to fetch detail for. Use "property-rates" for a CITY / LOCALITY / MICROMARKET's price, rates or market-insight page (market overview, price trends, locality/micromarket rates, rental rates, top projects + an AI narrative) — it ALSO requires `rateType` and the place's BEATS id (resolve it via search_entities first).

id.description:
The entity's NUMERIC id (e.g. "8761"), copied VERBATIM from a prior tool result — NEVER a name, slug, or guess ("piramal-revanta" is wrong). EXACTLY which field to copy, by entity:
• listing → the `id` field of a search_properties result.
• project → the `id` field of a search_projects result, OR a search_entities result whose type is "project" — use its `dotcomId` (project has a single id space; idType is not needed).
• developer → a search_entities result whose type is "builder" — use its `dotcomId`.
• city / locality / micromarket → a search_entities result of that type — use its `beatsId` (idType=beats, the default) or `dotcomId` (idType=dotcom).
If you only have a NAME, call the matching search tool FIRST and copy the id from the result you want — do not construct or transform it. Pick the result whose name (and city) matches the user's words before copying its id; if nothing clearly matches, say so rather than drilling a different entity.

idType.description: Which id space the id is from. Default beats. ONLY affects city/locality/micromarket (which have both id spaces). Ignored for developer/project/listing (single id) and property-rates (always beats). Pass dotcom when the id came from a dotcom-keyed field.

rateType.description: REQUIRED when entity="property-rates" (ignored otherwise): which kind of place the rate record is for — a city, locality, or micromarket (there is NO project rate page). Combined with the BEATS `id` it forms the key — e.g. rateType="city" + id="59" → Gurgaon city rates; rateType="micromarket" + id="154" → Vijayawada Central. Get the beats id by calling search_entities for the place FIRST and taking its `beatsId`.

fields.description: Optional top-level section(s) to return, COMMA-SEPARATED (e.g. "projectData,reraData"). Omit for the primary detail section, which already answers most questions. Examples — project: projectData (default; includes status, price, RERA wings + derived possessionStartingFrom), landmarks (nearby schools/hospitals/banks/metro by distance), reraData, keyAspects, stalledData. listing: listingData, landmarks (nearby points of interest by distance). city: cityData, topDevelopers, landmarks. locality/micromarket: localityOverviewData, insightsData, nearByLocalitiesV2, landmarks. developer: developerData. property-rates: propertyRatesData (structured rates) is the DEFAULT; add propertyRatesAiData to fields ONLY when the user wants the prose narrative (it is heavy and restates the numbers) — e.g. fields="propertyRatesData,propertyRatesAiData".

tools.name: compare_entities
tools.title: Compare Entities
tools.description: Compare 2-4 entities of the SAME type side by side (two projects, three localities, two listings), rendered as a comparison table. Pick this over calling get_entity_details repeatedly when the user asks to compare or contrast named places or properties. All items must share one `entity`, and you must already hold each numeric `id`: resolve each first via search_entities / search_properties / search_projects, never guessing. For city/locality/micromarket set `idType` to the id's source (beats default, or dotcom); it is ignored for project/listing. Cross-type comparison is not supported, and property-rates is not comparable. To RANK many localities or answer "which area is best" use recommend_localities.

entity.description: Entity type — the SAME for every item.

id.description: The entity's NUMERIC id, copied verbatim from a prior search/detail result.

idType.description: Id space (city/locality/micromarket only); default beats. Ignored otherwise.

items.description: The 2–4 entities to compare, ALL of the same `entity` type (e.g. two projects, or three localities). Resolve each id first via search_entities / search_properties / search_projects.

tools.name: recommend_localities
tools.title: Recommend & Rank Localities
tools.description: Rank 2-20 localities (or a city's top localities) for END-USE vs INVESTMENT, as a scored list. ROUTING: pick THIS when the user names MANY areas or asks for "the best area(s)" / a recommendation (compare_entities is only a 2-4 side-by-side TABLE and never ranks). Resolve each locality NAME to an id via search_entities (entityType="locality") FIRST, then pass `localities:[{id,idType}]` (or `cityId` to rank a city's top localities). Optional `budget` (absolute INR) flags each `inBudget`; `goal` = end_use | investment | both (default). HONEST + deterministic: it only combines signals get_entity_details already returns and NEVER invents a verdict. Sub-scores (0-100): connectivity/lifestyle/livability = the backend 0-5 index x20; appreciation = price-trend % (0%->50, +/-12.5%->100/0); liquidity (govt registered-deal volume) + value (rental yield) are ranked RELATIVE to the set. Weights - end-use: livability .35, connectivity .30, lifestyle .25, value .10; investment: appreciation .40, liquidity .30, value .20, connectivity .10; overall = their mean. A missing signal is OMITTED (not zero-filled), BUT a locality is only RANKED when present signals cover >50% of the goal's CORE (discriminating) weight — investment = appreciation/liquidity/yield (connectivity alone can't rank it), end-use = livability/connectivity/lifestyle; thinner ones go to `insufficientData` (with known signals + reason), so a one-signal locality can never top the list. signalCoverage is that CORE-weight share (0-1); each item also carries signalsUsed + raw numbers (avgRate, rentalYield, priceTrendPct, transactions) and VERBATIM pros/cons. India only, read-only.

id.description: The locality NUMERIC id, from a search_entities locality result.

idType.description: Id space of `id` (default beats). Pass "dotcom" when the id came from a dotcom-keyed field.

localities.description: The 2–20 localities to rank, each { id, idType? }. Resolve names → ids via search_entities (entityType="locality") FIRST; never guess. Provide this OR `cityId`.

cityId.description: Instead of an explicit list, rank the CITY's top localities (up to 15). A city id from search_entities. Ignored when `localities` is given.

budget.description: Optional purchase budget, absolute INR (e.g. {min:20000000,max:30000000}). Flags each locality `inBudget` when a real project there fits — never a hard filter.

bedrooms.description: Optional BHK context, e.g. "3 BHK" (echoed; the ranking is locality-level).

goal.description: Which composite sorts the result: end_use (livability/connectivity), investment (appreciation/liquidity/yield), or both (default).

tools.name: search_faq
tools.title: Search Real-Estate FAQ
tools.description: Answer INFORMATIONAL/advisory real-estate questions -- buying/renting/selling process, home loans, legal, RERA rights, NRI purchases, Azuro-managed rentals -- from the bundled Square Yards FAQ corpus. Pick this for general how/what/why questions; needs NO id, does NOT touch listings/projects. Do NOT use it to find inventory (use search_entities -> search_properties/search_projects), for a PLACE-specific price/rates question (use get_entity_details entity="property-rates"), or for EMI/affordability NUMBERS (use estimate_home_loan, not this). Optionally pass `category` (e.g. buying/renting/selling) to scope results; `top_k` caps returned Q/A pairs (default 3).

query.description: An informational question, e.g. "what credit score do I need for a home loan".

category.description: Optional: scope the search to one FAQ category (e.g. "buying", "renting", "selling"). Matched on the category id or label, case-insensitive. If it does not match a known category the filter is ignored and a note lists the valid ones.

tools.name: estimate_home_loan
tools.title: Home Loan EMI & Affordability Calculator
tools.description: Calculate a home-loan EMI, or estimate how much a buyer can afford, for INDIA home loans. mode="emi": given loanAmount (or propertyPrice + down payment) + rate + tenure, returns the monthly EMI, total interest and total payable. mode="affordability": given monthly/annual NET income (+ existing EMIs, optional down-payment cash), returns the max EMI capacity, max loan and max property price via FOIR + RBI LTV tiers. Use THIS for any loan NUMBERS question ("EMI on X", "what can I afford on Y salary", "how much down payment do I need") — e.g. turn a listing/project card price into an EMI. For loan PROCESS/documents/eligibility prose use search_faq instead. Pure calculator: no ids, no live data. Money is absolute INR (1.2 Cr → 12000000). Defaults: 8.75% p.a., 20-year tenure, FOIR 0.50, stamp+registration ≈6%. Results are indicative with the disclaimer included — never present them as a loan offer.

mode.description: "emi" = monthly payment for a known loan/price; "affordability" = max budget from income.

loanAmount.description: emi mode: loan principal in absolute INR (₹80L → 8000000). Wins over propertyPrice.

propertyPrice.description: emi mode: property price in absolute INR — the loan is price minus down payment.

downPayment.description: emi mode: down payment in absolute INR (used with propertyPrice).

downPaymentPercent.description: emi mode: down payment as % of propertyPrice; used when downPayment is absent. If neither is given the RBI-minimum down payment for the price band is assumed.

monthlyIncome.description: affordability mode: NET take-home income per month, absolute INR (₹2L → 200000).

annualIncome.description: affordability mode: NET annual income, absolute INR (divided by 12 internally).

existingEmi.description: affordability mode: existing monthly EMI obligations, INR (default 0).

foir.description: affordability mode: share of income lenders allow for all EMIs (default 0.50; clamped 0.3–0.6).

downPaymentAvailable.description: affordability mode: cash available for down payment + costs — caps the max property price.

includeTxnCosts.description: Include ~6% stamp duty + registration in the cash estimates (default true).

tools.name: area_conversion
tools.title: Area Unit Converter
tools.description: Convert a land/area measurement between the units used in INDIA — metric (sq metre, sq km, hectare, are, sq cm), imperial (sq feet, sq yard/"gaj", sq inch, acre) and traditional Indian land units (cent, decimal, ground, guntha, marla, kanal, killa, ankanam, bigha, biswa, kattha). Use THIS for any unit-conversion NUMBERS ("how many sq ft in a bigha", "convert 5 acre to gaj", "200 gaj in sq feet"). Pure calculator — no ids, no live data. Pass `value` (a positive number) and `from`; give `to` for a single target, or omit it to get the value in the common units at once. Units accept friendly aliases (sqft, sqm, gaj, acre, cent, ground…). IMPORTANT: bigha, biswa and kattha differ by state, so pass a state-qualified code (BIGHA_PUCCA_UP_I, BISWA_HP_I, KATTHA_BIHAR, …); a bare "bigha" or an unknown unit returns the list of valid codes. For property PRICE/EMI numbers use estimate_home_loan; for live listings use search_properties.

value.description: The area amount to convert — a positive number, e.g. 5 for "5 acre".

from.description: Source unit. Codes or aliases: SQ_M, SQ_FT, SQ_YD ("gaj"), SQ_CM, SQ_IN, SQ_KM, HECTARE, ARE, ACRE, CENT, DECIMAL, GROUND, GUNTHA, MARLA, KANAL, KILLA, ANKANAM; bigha/biswa/kattha are state-qualified (e.g. BIGHA_PUCCA_UP_I, BISWA_HP_I, KATTHA_BIHAR).

to.description: Target unit (same code/alias set). OMIT to get the value in the common units (ft², yd², m², acre, hectare) at once.
